title: Boss build: Guess the number
hook: Build a real game: the computer hides a number and you hunt it down.

warmup.q: What does `for i in range(3): print(i)` show?
warmup.explain: range(3) gives three numbers starting at 0: 0, 1, 2. The stop number is never included.

warmup.q: `hour = 20`. Is `hour >= 6 and hour < 18` True or False?
warmup.explain: With and, BOTH sides must be True. 20 >= 6 is True, but 20 < 18 is False. So the whole thing is False.
int() turns the text "4" into the number 4, so adding 1 gives 5. Without int, text plus a number is an error.

why.heading: Today you build a real game
why.text: Friday is boss day. The computer secretly picks a number from 1 to 20. You guess. It says too low or too high. You keep going until you get it. Every game is just two things you already know: loops and decisions. We build it in 3 steps, and step 3 is the finished game.

why.heading: import: borrow a toolbox
why.text: Python cannot pick random numbers by itself. It has a toolbox called `random` that someone else wrote. Borrow it with `import random` at the top. Then `random.randint(1, 20)` gives a whole number from 1 to 20, and BOTH ends can come up. This is different from `range`, which stops before the end.

why.heading: The game loop
why.text: Every guessing game follows one recipe: ask for a guess, compare it with the secret (`if`, `elif`), and go round again until it is right (`while`). Say it in plain words first, then turn each part into one piece of code.

why.heading: Counting tries
why.text: Make a counter before the loop: `tries = 0`. Inside the loop, `tries += 1` after every guess. Then you can stop after 5 tries with `while guess != secret and tries < 5:`. Two questions joined by `and`: not guessed yet, AND still tries left.

why.heading: A seed makes random testable
why.text: How can the checker mark a game that is random? With a **seed**: a starting point for the dice. Same seed, same number every time. The checker uses a fixed seed so it knows the secret. In the tasks, treat the secret as unknown and guess low and high. In your own game there is no seed.

watch.intro: Tap Run. The computer rolls a die. Notice the first line: `import random`.
watch.code:
import random

roll = random.randint(1, 6)
print(f"You rolled a {roll}")
if roll == 6:
    print("Six! Roll again")
else:
    print("Not a six")
explain: `import random` opens the toolbox. It goes at the top, before you use it.
`random.randint(1, 6)` picks a whole number from 1 to 6 and stores it in `roll`.
After that it is an ordinary if and else, just like Day 6.
watch.break_it: Break it on purpose: delete the line `import random` and run. You get `NameError: name 'random' is not defined` on line 3. Python does not know the toolbox until you import it. Put the line back.

tasks.title: Step 1: one guess
tasks.task: The secret is already picked. Ask `Your guess? `, then compare: show `Too low` if the guess is under the secret, `Too high` if over, or `Correct!` if equal. (The checker uses a fixed secret. Just write the comparison.)
tasks.starter:
import random
secret = random.randint(1, 20)
guess = int(input("Your guess? "))
# add your if, elif and else here
hints: Three roads: below the secret, above the secret, or neither (so it must be equal).
if guess < secret: ... elif guess > secret: ... else: ...  Each with a pushed-in print.

tasks.title: Step 2: keep guessing
tasks.task: Now keep asking until the guess is right. After each wrong guess show `Too low` or `Too high`. When it is right, show `Correct!` once, after the loop. Start `guess` at 0 so the loop begins.
tasks.starter:
import random
secret = random.randint(1, 20)
guess = 0
# add your while loop here
print("Correct!")
hints: The loop runs while the guess is not equal to the secret: while guess != secret:
Inside the loop: ask with input, then the if / elif from step 1 (no else this time).

Your guess? 15

Your guess? 1
Too low
Your guess? 12

tasks.title: Step 3: the finished game
tasks.task: Make it the full game. Show `Guess my number, 1 to 20` first. Count the tries. Allow 5 tries at most. Win: show `You win! Tries: 3` (with the real number). Out of tries: show `Out of tries. It was 11` (with the real secret). Drop the `Correct!` line.
hints: Add tries = 0 before the loop and tries += 1 inside it, right after the guess.
Loop condition: while guess != secret and tries < 5:  After the loop, an if / else decides the ending message.
After the loop: if guess == secret: print(f"You win! Tries: {tries}") else: print(f"Out of tries. It was {secret}")

recap: `import random` borrows the toolbox. `random.randint(1, 20)` picks 1 to 20, both ends included.
A guessing game is: ask, compare, repeat until right.
A counter (`tries += 1`) inside the loop counts the rounds.
`while a and b:` keeps looping only while BOTH are True.
A seed makes random repeatable, so tests can check it.

words.meaning: Borrow a ready-made toolbox of code for your program.
Picks a whole number between two numbers, both included.
A starting point for random. Same seed gives the same numbers every time.
The repeating ask, check, respond cycle at the heart of a game.
